title: ISO 45001:2018 Internal Auditor — Capstone Exam
instrument_notice: This is a knowledge-underpinning assessment measuring recognition of correct audit reasoning, not the generative skills of live audit practice.
extraction_note: This 65-question pool feeds a stratified, category-aware extractor presenting 35 questions per sitting.

paragraphs: Paragraph 1: Apex Heavy Engineering, a manufacturer of industrial turbines, is undergoing its annual internal OH&S audit. The facility recently expanded its operations by introducing a new automated welding line. External regulatory changes regarding occupational exposure limits to welding fumes were enacted three months prior to the audit.

Paragraph 2: During the document review phase, the internal auditor examines the OH&S hazard identification and risk assessment (HIRA) register. The register was last updated 14 months ago. The auditor notes that the new automated welding line is not explicitly detailed in the current HIRA, though 'general welding' is listed.

Paragraph 3: Proceeding to fieldwork, the auditor interviews a technician, Sarah, operating the new welding line. Sarah mentions that the local exhaust ventilation (LEV) system frequently trips and shuts down. When asked about reporting this, she states she mentioned it to her supervisor, but there is no formal hazard report filed.

Paragraph 4: The auditor cross-references the maintenance logs for the LEV system with the shift handover notes. The maintenance logs show no reported faults, but the shift handover notes from the past two weeks indicate 'ventilation reset required' on six separate occasions.

Paragraph 5: Synthesizing the evidence, the auditor identifies a significant gap: an uncontrolled change in process (the new line) without an updated risk assessment, compounded by untrained personnel bypassing failing safety controls (the LEV system) without utilizing the formal incident reporting procedure.

Paragraph 6: Applying the Five-Whys technique, the auditor traces the root cause. Why was the LEV tripped? (Filter overload). Why did it overload? (The new line generates double the particulate volume). Why wasn't this anticipated? (Management of Change procedure was bypassed). Why was it bypassed? (The project manager categorized it as an 'equipment replacement' rather than a 'process change').

Paragraph 7: The Production Manager proposes an immediate containment action: purchasing higher-capacity filters for the LEV and instructing Sarah to submit a hazard report. The auditor notes this addresses the immediate symptom but fails to investigate the systemic failure of the Management of Change (MoC) process.

Paragraph 8: The auditor prepares the final report, classifying the finding based on the potential severity of prolonged fume exposure and the high likelihood of recurrence due to the flawed MoC process. The findings are compiled for presentation at the upcoming Management Review meeting.

finding_severity_matrix.description: Severity model: Score = Potential Harm x Likelihood of Recurrence.

questions.text: Based on Paragraph 1, sort the following audit context factors into their respective categories under ISO 45001 Clause 4.1 (Context) and 4.2 (Interested Parties).

items.text: Changes to regulatory occupational exposure limits

questions.rationale: Auditors must distinguish between conditions (issues) and entities (parties).
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 2.1 — Context of the Organization.

questions.text: Arrange the steps the auditor took to establish the evidence trail regarding the LEV failure in chronological order.

steps.text: Review maintenance logs for documented system faults
Interview Sarah regarding daily operational issues
Cross-reference shift handover notes for informal workarounds

questions.rationale: The trail started with an interview, moved to formal logs, and concluded with informal notes.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 4.3 — Collecting and Verifying Audit Evidence.

questions.text: Complete the Nonconformity Report for the primary systemic failure observed.

tool_data.findings: A new automated welding line was introduced without completing a risk assessment prior to implementation.

questions.rationale: The systemic breakdown was failing to follow Management of Change before introducing new equipment.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 6.2 — Writing Nonconformity Reports.

questions.text: Trace the observed audit failure to its systemic root cause using Five Whys.

levels.question: Why did the local exhaust ventilation (LEV) trip?
Why wasn't the increased volume anticipated?
options: HIRA register was out of date

levels.question: Why was the MoC procedure bypassed?

questions.rationale: RCA must trace past the physical failure to the management system failure.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 7.1 — Root Cause Analysis Techniques.

questions.text: The external regulatory changes to occupational exposure limits represent which element of the OH&S management system?

options.text: A legal and other requirement under Clause 6.1.3
A hazard identification opportunity under Clause 6.1.2

questions.rationale: Regulatory changes directly form part of legal and other requirements that the organization must comply with.

questions.text: True or False: Relying on 'general welding' in the HIRA register is sufficient for the new automated line since the core activity is similar.
questions.rationale: New equipment introduces new hazards (like higher fume volumes) requiring specific risk assessment updates.

questions.text: Sarah's failure to file a formal hazard report indicates a potential weakness in which area?

options.text: Clause 5.4 Consultation and participation of workers

questions.rationale: Workers must be aware of how to report incidents and hazards, pointing to awareness and communication gaps.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 4.2 — Awareness and Communication.

questions.text: The discrepancy between maintenance logs and shift handover notes demonstrates the auditor's use of:
questions.rationale: Comparing multiple sources of information to verify facts is triangulation.

questions.text: True or False: The primary breakdown observed in Paragraph 5 is solely a failure of operator competence (Clause 7.2).
questions.rationale: The root issue is a systemic failure in Management of Change (8.1.3), not just operator competence.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 5.3 — Management of Change.

questions.text: Categorizing the new line as an 'equipment replacement' rather than a 'process change' bypassed which critical step?

options.text: Proactive risk assessment of the change

questions.rationale: Management of Change ensures new hazards are assessed before implementation.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 5.3 — Management of Change.

questions.text: The Production Manager's proposal to purchase higher-capacity filters is classified as:
questions.rationale: It fixes the immediate problem but not the process failure that caused it.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 7.2 — Nonconformity and Corrective Action.

questions.text: True or False: The auditor is responsible for designing the corrective action plan to fix the MoC process.
questions.rationale: Auditors report findings; the auditee is responsible for determining and implementing corrective actions.

questions.text: What type of audit evidence is the HIRA register?
questions.rationale: Registers and records are classified as documented information.

questions.text: Sarah reporting the issue verbally but not formally indicates a breakdown in what OH&S system requirement?
questions.rationale: Failing to utilize the formal reporting structure indicates internal communication processes are ineffective.

questions.text: If the auditor accepts the Production Manager's containment as the final corrective action, what principle is violated?

options.text: Addressing the root cause to prevent recurrence

questions.rationale: Clause 10.2 requires evaluating the need for action to eliminate root causes.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 7.2 — Root Cause Analysis.

questions.text: An auditor finds hazard assessments are conducted solely by the Safety Manager. Which clause is compromised?

options.text: Clause 5.4 Consultation and participation of workers

questions.rationale: Clause 5.4 requires participation of non-managerial workers in identifying hazards.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an external issue relevant to the OH&S management system?
questions.rationale: National labor laws are external factors affecting the organization.

questions.text: True or False: The organization must document every single interested party, regardless of relevance to the OH&S system.
questions.rationale: Only interested parties that are relevant to the OH&S management system need to be determined.

questions.text: When determining the scope of the OH&S management system, the organization must consider:

options.text: Issues, interested parties, and planned work activities
Only the physical boundaries of the site

questions.rationale: Scope determination requires inputs from 4.1 (issues), 4.2 (parties), and activities performed.

questions.text: Clause 4.4 requires the organization to establish, implement, maintain, and continually improve:

options.text: The OH&S management system and its processes

questions.rationale: Clause 4.4 mandates the process approach for the OH&S system.

questions.text: True or False: Top management can completely delegate accountability for the effectiveness of the OH&S management system to the Safety Manager.
questions.rationale: Top management must take overall responsibility and accountability; it cannot be delegated.

questions.text: The OH&S policy must include a commitment to:

options.text: Eliminate hazards and reduce OH&S risks

questions.rationale: Eliminating hazards and reducing risks is a mandatory commitment in the policy.

questions.text: True or False: ISO 45001 requires organizations to maintain documented information of their legal and other requirements.
questions.rationale: Clause 6.1.3 mandates maintaining documented information on legal requirements.

questions.text: Hazard identification processes should consider which of the following?

options.text: Activities that have previously caused injury

questions.rationale: Hazard ID must be proactive and cover all types of situations and activities.

questions.text: When assessing OH&S risks, the organization must consider:

options.text: Only the severity of potential injury

questions.rationale: Risk assessment involves evaluating risk while taking into account the effectiveness of current controls.

questions.text: True or False: Planning actions must address risks, opportunities, and legal requirements, and integrate them into OH&S processes.
questions.rationale: Clause 6.1.4 requires integrating planned actions into the system processes.

questions.text: OH&S objectives must be:

options.text: Measurable (if practicable) and consistent with the OH&S policy

questions.rationale: Objectives must align with policy commitments and be measurable where possible.

questions.text: When planning how to achieve OH&S objectives, the organization must determine:

options.text: What will be done, resources required, responsibility, and timeframe

questions.rationale: Clause 6.2.2 explicitly lists what, resources, who, when, and how results are evaluated.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 3.6 — Planning to Achieve.

questions.text: A facility considers hazards from a neighboring chemical plant. Is this required?

options.text: Yes, hazards occurring in the vicinity that can affect people in the workplace must be considered.
No, neighbor hazards are a regulatory issue.
Only if they share a common wall.

questions.rationale: Clause 6.1.2.1 (e) requires considering hazards in the vicinity of the workplace.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 3.3 — Hazard Identification Scope.

questions.text: True or False: OH&S opportunities include adapting work, work organization, and work environments to workers.
questions.rationale: Adapting work to workers is a core example of an OH&S opportunity (6.1.2.3).

questions.text: An organization relies on PPE instead of enclosing a noisy machine. How does this relate to Clause 8.1.2?

options.text: Nonconformant, as engineering controls should be prioritized over PPE.
Conformant if workers sign a waiver.
Nonconformant because machines cannot be enclosed.

questions.rationale: The hierarchy of controls dictates engineering controls before PPE.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 5.2 — Hierarchy of Controls.

questions.text: True or False: Operational criteria for processes must be established and implemented to eliminate hazards and reduce OH&S risks.
questions.rationale: Establishing operational criteria is required for effective process control.

questions.text: A facility changes its shift pattern from 8 to 12 hours. Under ISO 45001, what must happen first?

options.text: Review the OH&S risks associated with the change (MoC)

questions.rationale: Changes to working conditions (shifts) require Management of Change assessment.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 5.3 — Management of Change.

questions.text: When purchasing a new chemical, the organization must:

options.text: Ensure procurement processes control OH&S impacts of the product

questions.rationale: Procurement processes must identify and control OH&S risks of purchased goods.

questions.text: True or False: Organizations are not responsible for the OH&S risks caused by contractors’ activities on their site.
questions.rationale: Organizations must coordinate procurement processes with contractors to manage hazards.

questions.text: If an organization outsources its maintenance department, it must:

options.text: Ensure outsourced functions are controlled within the OH&S system
Exclude them from the OH&S scope

questions.rationale: Outsourced processes affecting the OH&S system must be controlled.

questions.text: Emergency preparedness requires the organization to:

options.text: Maintain a planned response to potential emergency situations

questions.rationale: A planned response to identified emergency situations is a core requirement.

questions.text: True or False: Emergency response plans must be periodically tested and the results evaluated.
questions.rationale: Clause 8.2 (d) explicitly requires periodic testing and exercise of emergency capabilities.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 5.5 — Testing Emergency Plans.

questions.text: What is the highest level of control in the Hierarchy of Controls?
questions.rationale: Elimination is the most effective control and sits at the top of the hierarchy.

questions.text: Replacing a toxic solvent with a water-based alternative is an example of:
questions.rationale: Replacing a hazard with a less hazardous alternative is substitution.

questions.text: True or False: The organization's OH&S requirements must be communicated to contractors.
questions.rationale: Clause 8.1.4.2 requires defining and communicating OH&S criteria to contractors.

questions.text: Providing first aid training to designated workers supports which requirement?
questions.rationale: Training for emergency response is explicitly required under Clause 8.2.

questions.text: True or False: Equipment calibration records do not need to be retained if maintained by a certified third party.
questions.rationale: Clause 9.1.1 requires retaining documented info of monitoring results, regardless of who calibrates.

questions.text: An HR Manager audits the HR department's training records. What is the primary issue?
questions.rationale: Auditors must be impartial and not audit their own work.

questions.text: The organization must determine what needs to be monitored and measured, including:

options.text: The extent to which legal requirements are fulfilled

questions.rationale: Fulfillment of legal and other requirements is a mandatory monitoring criterion.

questions.text: True or False: The organization must establish a process to evaluate compliance with legal and other requirements.
questions.rationale: Clause 9.1.2 mandates a process for evaluating compliance.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 6.2 — Evaluation of Compliance.

questions.text: An internal audit program must be planned considering:

options.text: The importance of the processes concerned and previous audit results
When the CEO is on vacation

questions.rationale: Audit programs must be risk-based, considering process importance and past results.

questions.text: Which of the following is a mandatory input for the Management Review?

options.text: Results of worker participation and consultation
Detailed maintenance schedules for next year

questions.rationale: Worker participation results are explicitly listed in 9.3 (d)(3).
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 6.4 — Management Review Inputs.

questions.text: True or False: Management review outputs must include decisions related to continual improvement opportunities.
questions.rationale: Decisions on continual improvement are a required output of management review.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 6.4 — Management Review Outputs.

questions.text: Documented information for monitoring and measurement is required as evidence of:
questions.rationale: Evidence of monitoring and measurement results must be retained.

questions.text: Fixing a broken safety guard immediately is an example of:
questions.rationale: Correction addresses the immediate symptom. Corrective action addresses the root cause (why it broke).
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 7.2 — Correction vs Corrective Action.

questions.text: True or False: Organizations must determine opportunities for improvement and implement necessary actions.
questions.rationale: Clause 10.1 establishes the general requirement for continual improvement actions.

questions.text: When an incident occurs, the organization must first:

options.text: React in a timely manner and deal with the consequences

questions.rationale: Immediate reaction (containment/correction) is the first step required by 10.2.

questions.text: Investigating the root cause of an incident is necessary to:

options.text: Ensure it does not recur or occur elsewhere
Assign blame to a specific worker

questions.rationale: The purpose of RCA is to eliminate causes to prevent recurrence.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 7.3 — Root Cause Analysis.

questions.text: True or False: Corrective actions must be reviewed for effectiveness after they are implemented.
questions.rationale: Evaluating the effectiveness of action taken is a strict requirement of 10.2(e).

questions.text: Continual improvement of the OH&S management system should primarily aim to:

options.text: Enhance OH&S performance and promote a positive culture
Eliminate the need for management review

questions.rationale: Enhancing OH&S performance and culture are primary intents of continual improvement.

questions.text: Who must be communicated with regarding the results of incident investigations?
questions.rationale: Clause 10.2 requires communicating results to relevant workers and representatives.

questions.text: True or False: OH&S risks do not need to be reassessed if a corrective action introduces a new control.
questions.rationale: Clause 10.2 (d) requires reviewing existing OH&S risk assessments prior to taking action.

questions.text: What type of documented information must be retained following a nonconformity?

options.text: Evidence of the nature of the NC and subsequent actions taken
None, if it was fixed immediately

questions.rationale: Records must reflect the nature of the issue, actions taken, and effectiveness results.

questions.text: During an investigation, why is it necessary to determine if similar nonconformities exist elsewhere?

options.text: To apply systemic corrective actions across the organization
To find more people to blame
To increase the audit finding severity

questions.rationale: Clause 10.2 requires the organization to review the effectiveness of any corrective action taken. Documenting 'action taken' is not enough; there must be evidence that the action actually eliminated the root cause and prevented recurrence.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 7.3 — Systemic Corrective Action.

questions.text: As the Lead Auditor preparing for the Apex Manufacturing surveillance audit, build a targeted Audit Plan for the newly acquired Plant B by assigning the correct fragments to the plan template.

fragments.text: Verify the effectiveness of hazard identification and operational controls for the newly integrated high-speed packaging line.
Confirm the financial ROI and production output quotas of the Plant B acquisition.
Clause 8.1.3 (Management of change) and Clause 6.1.2 (Hazard identification).
Clause 4.3 (Determining the scope of the OHSMS) and Clause 9.2 (Internal audit).
Packaging Line Machine Operators and the Plant Manager.

questions.rationale: An effective OH&S audit plan must have clear safety objectives (verifying controls for the new equipment), target the relevant standard requirements (MOC and Hazard ID), and identify the personnel actually exposed to the risk.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 4.1 — Audit Planning and Scoping.

questions.text: Based on the Apex Manufacturing scenario, build the Nonconformity Report (NCR) regarding the bypassed safety guard on the new high-speed packaging line.

fragments.text: Clause 8.1.3 - Management of Change
Clause 5.1 - Leadership and commitment
During the floor tour, a machine operator was observed running the newly installed high-speed packaging line with the physical safety guard completely bypassed.
The worker was fearful of being disciplined for missing production quotas.
The organization failed to implement and control planned changes to mitigate OH&S risks prior to equipment handover, resulting in operators bypassing poorly integrated controls.

questions.rationale: A legally sound NCR must state the exact ISO 45001 requirement breached, present undeniable factual evidence (the bypassed guard), and clearly state the systemic failure (MOC bypass).

questions.text: The Plant Manager has submitted a Corrective Action Plan (CAP) in response to the bypassed guard. Reconstruct the approved CAP to ensure it addresses the systemic root cause.

fragments.text: Stop the machine, repair the jammed safety guard, and re-induct the specific operator.
The technician was careless and deliberately ignored safety protocols to finish their shift early.
The Management of Change (MOC) process was expedited for a major client order, bypassing formal hazard reviews and training protocols.
Revise the MOC procedure to require a mandatory EHS hard-stop sign-off and competency verification on all relocated equipment before production handover.
Reprimand the operator and issue a written warning to all Plant B staff.

questions.rationale: A robust OH&S CAP must separate immediate fixes (Correction) from the underlying procedural flaws (Root Cause). The long-term action must fix the systemic process (MOC revision), not just discipline the worker.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 10.2 — Evaluating Corrective Actions.

questions.text: The Lead Auditor is verifying if Apex Manufacturing is prepared for its upcoming Top Management Review. Build the agenda by dragging the correct ISO 45001 mandatory inputs and expected outputs into the template.

fragments.text: Results of consultation and participation of workers, including safety committee feedback.
A detailed review of the daily cafeteria menu and parking lot allocations.
Information on OH&S performance, including trends in incidents, nonconformities, and corrective actions.
Decisions related to continual improvement opportunities and any needed changes to the OH&S management system or resources.
A finalized product marketing strategy for the upcoming fiscal year.

questions.rationale: Clause 9.3 mandates specific inputs unique to ISO 45001 (like worker consultation results and incident trends) and outputs (decisions on continual improvement). Identifying these separates a formal OH&S Management Review from a standard operational meeting.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 9.3 — Management Review Requirements.

questions.text: Review the following audit findings from various departments. Classify the severity of each and map it to the most appropriate ISO 45001 clause.

tool_data.instructions: Select 5 random findings from the pool below for the candidate to evaluate.

findings_pool.evidence: Top management has delegated all OH&S accountability to the HR Manager and refuses to participate in safety walkarounds or management reviews.
An auditor discovers a company policy that penalizes workers' annual bonuses if they report near-miss incidents, creating a culture of underreporting.
First aid kits located in the hazardous chemical storage area are fully stocked, sealed, and inspected monthly by the safety officer.
A review of the HIRA (Hazard Identification) register shows that routine daily operations are well documented, but non-routine maintenance activities are entirely omitted.
One out of eighty employees in the fabrication department missed the monthly safety toolbox talk due to being on annual leave.
External roof-repair contractors are observed working at height without fall protection. The site manager admits they do not review the safety records or procedures of outsourced labor.
Noise exposure dosimeter monitoring is conducted exactly according to the planned schedule, and all calibration records for the equipment are securely maintained.
Following a minor forklift collision last month, the organization repaired the forklift but closed the incident report without investigating the root cause or taking action to prevent recurrence.
The organization's context analysis identifies a rapidly aging workforce as an internal issue, but no OH&S risks or ergonomic controls were derived from this analysis.

Fire evacuation drills are conducted annually; however, the facility has never conducted a drill simulating a medical emergency or confined space rescue, despite those being their highest-rated risks.
The organization successfully substituted a highly toxic cleaning solvent with a safe, water-based alternative, eliminating the need for complex respirators.
During the internal audit, the Production Manager was observed auditing the safety controls of their own production line.
Safety committee minutes show that a severe tripping hazard on the stairs was reported by workers three months ago, but no action has been taken to address it.
An evacuation drill was conducted successfully within the targeted time limit, but there is no documented record of management evaluating the drill's effectiveness to seek improvements.

The organization relies entirely on an external consultant to determine its OH&S compliance obligations. The consultant hasn't updated the legal register to reflect new national machinery safety laws enacted two years ago.

questions.rationale: An internal auditor must demonstrate the ability to rapidly assess varied OH&S evidence, distinguishing between critical safety/systemic failures (Major NC), isolated procedural lapses (Minor NC), and compliant operational behaviors.
questions.lms_direction: Review LMS Activity 7.1 — Evidence Evaluation and Classification.
